'''Heino Falcke''' (born 26 September 1966 in [[Cologne]]) is a German professor of [[radio astronomy]] and [[astroparticle physics]] at the [[Radboud University Nijmegen]] (Netherlands).<ref name="nwo">{{cite web |author= |date=26 August 2014 |title=Prof. H.D.E. (Heino) Falcke |url=http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/heino+falcke |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304140441/http://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/spinoza+prize/spinoza+laureates/overview+in+alphabetical+order/heino+falcke |archive-date=4 March 2016 |access-date=25 July 2015 |publisher=[[Netherlands Organisation for Scientific Research]]}}</ref> His main field of study is [[black hole]]s, and he is the originator of the concept of the 'black hole shadow'.<ref name=":0" /> In 2019, Falcke announced the first [[Event Horizon Telescope]] results at the EHT Press Conference in Brussels.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=April 2019|title=Media Advisory: First Results from the Event Horizon Telescope to be Presented on April 10th|url=https://eventhorizontelescope.org/blog/media-advisory-first-results-event-horizon-telescope-be-presented-april-10th|access-date=|website=}}</ref>

==Career==
Falcke studied physics at the [[University of Cologne]] from 1986 to 1987, and then at the [[University of Bonn]] from 1987 where he graduated with a [[Diplom]]a (equivalent to a master's degree) in Physics in 1992. He subsequently obtained a PhD degree in Astronomy ''[[summa cum laude]]'' in 1994 from the University of Bonn.<ref name=nwo/><ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Hungernde Löcher und aktive Kerne: die zentrale Maschine in galaktischen Zentren |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=idn=942216822 |first=Heino |last=Falcke}}</ref>

Falcke subsequently worked as a scientist for the [[Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy]] in Bonn (1995–1995), the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] (1995–1997), and the [[University of Arizona]] (1999).<ref name="nwo" /> He was conferred a [[Habilitation]] by the University of Bonn in 2000.<ref>[https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Falcke_Heino/CV Heino Falcke – Curriculum Vitae] – website of [[Academia Europaea]]</ref> From 2000 to 2003, he was a staff scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy]] in Bonn.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2020 |title=Heino Falcke is a theoretical astrophysicist and radio astronomer |url=https://heinofalcke.org/ |access-date=14 November 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Academy of Europe: Falcke Heino |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Falcke_Heino |access-date=14 November 2023 |website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref>

In 2003, Falcke became adjunct professor of Radio Astronomy and Astroparticle physics at [[Radboud University Nijmegen]]. He also started working for [[ASTRON]], the radio astronomy institute of the Netherlands. In 2007, he became a full professor at Nijmegen.<ref name=nwo/>

==Research==
Falcke is involved in theoretical astronomy as well as observational and experimental studies.<ref name=radboud>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.ru.nl/onderzoek/over/onderzoeksthema/sterrenkunde/sterrenkunde/heino-falcke-spinoza/ |title=Heino Falcke kijkt verder dan de horizon van het zwarte gat |language=Dutch |publisher=Radboud University Nijmegen |date= |access-date=26 July 2015 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Falcke was one of the leading forces behind the radio telescope [[Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR)|LOFAR]].<ref name="nwo" /><ref name="astron">{{cite web |author= |date=7 June 2011 |title=Heino Falcke receives highest Dutch scientific award |url=https://www.astron.nl/about-astron/press-public/news/heino-falcke-receives-highest-dutch-scientific-award/heino-falcke-rec |access-date=25 July 2015 |publisher=ASTRON |language=Dutch |archive-date=9 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709170923/http://www.astron.nl/about-astron/press-public/news/heino-falcke-receives-highest-dutch-scientific-award/heino-falcke-rec |url-status=dead }}</ref> Apart from his work with [[Low-Frequency Array (LOFAR)|LOFAR]], he was also involved in the development of the [[Square Kilometre Array]].<ref name=radboud/>

In 2000 he predicted it would be possible to make measurements near the edge of a black hole. Four years later, his team managed to do that.<ref name=radboud/>

In 2013, Falcke, together with [[Luciano Rezzolla]] of the [[Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics]] proposed that [[blitzar]]s could be an explanation for [[fast radio burst]]s.<ref>{{cite magazine|author=Govert Schilling |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn23817-mystery-radio-bursts-blamed-on-black-hole-blitzars/ |title=Mystery radio bursts blamed on black hole 'blitzars' |magazine=[[New Scientist]] |date=4 July 2013 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref> Blitzars would occur when a supramassive rotating [[neutron star]] slows down enough, loses its magnetic field, and then turns into a black hole.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.ru.nl/@894031/afscheidsgroet/ |title=Afscheidsgroet van een stervende ster |language=Dutch |publisher=Radboud University Nijmegen |date=4 July 2013 |access-date=26 July 2015 |archive-date=10 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200110191025/https://www.ru.nl/@894031/afscheidsgroet/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=John Timmer |url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2013/07/possible-explanation-for-radio-bursts-meet-the-blitzar/ |title=Possible explanation for radio bursts: Meet the "blitzar" |language=Dutch |website=[[Ars Technica]] |date=8 July 2013 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref>

Falcke predicted that near the edges of a black hole, there would be a 'black hole shadow' that could be detected by a radio telescope.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Falcke|first1=Heino|last2=Melia|first2=Fulvio|last3=Agol|first3=Eric|date=1 January 2000|title=Viewing the Shadow of the Black Hole at the Galactic Center|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1086/312423|journal=The Astrophysical Journal|volume=528|issue=1|pages=L13–L16|doi=10.1086/312423|pmid=10587484|arxiv=astro-ph/9912263|bibcode=2000ApJ...528L..13F|s2cid=119433133}}</ref><ref name="astron" /> This shadow was eventually observed with the [[Event Horizon Telescope]]. On 10 April 2019, the project announced that they created an image of the black hole at the centre of [[Messier 87|M87]] ([[M87*]]).<ref>{{cite news |title=First ever black hole image released |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-47873592 |access-date=11 April 2019}}</ref> On 12 May 2022 followed the image of the central black hole in the [[Milky Way]] ([[Sagittarius A*]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hensley |first=Kerry |date=12 May 2022 |title=First Image of the Milky Way's Supermassive Black Hole |url=https://aasnova.org/2022/05/12/first-image-of-the-milky-ways-supermassive-black-hole/ |access-date=14 November 2023 |website=AAS Nova |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Collaboration |first1=Event Horizon Telescope |last2=Akiyama |first2=Kazunori |last3=Alberdi |first3=Antxon |last4=Alef |first4=Walter |last5=Algaba |first5=Juan Carlos |last6=Anantua |first6=Richard |last7=Asada |first7=Keiichi |last8=Azulay |first8=Rebecca |last9=Bach |first9=Uwe |last10=Baczko |first10=Anne-Kathrin |last11=Ball |first11=David |last12=Baloković |first12=Mislav |last13=Barrett |first13=John |last14=Bauböck |first14=Michi |last15=Benson |first15=Bradford A. |date=May 2022 |title=First Sagittarius A* Event Horizon Telescope Results. III. Imaging of the Galactic Center Supermassive Black Hole |journal=The Astrophysical Journal Letters |language=en |volume=930 |issue=2 |pages=L14 |doi=10.3847/2041-8213/ac6429 |issn=2041-8205|doi-access=free |arxiv=2311.09479 |bibcode=2022ApJ...930L..14E }}</ref>

Falcke wishes to place a radio telescope on the [[Moon]] and has worked with [[NASA]] and [[European Space Agency]] researchers to devise a plan to make this happen.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jester |first1=Sebastian |last2=Falcke |first2=Heino |date=May 2009 |title=Science with a lunar low-frequency array: from the dark ages of the Universe to nearby exoplanets |journal=New Astronomy Reviews |volume=53 |issue=1–2 |pages=1–26 |doi=10.1016/j.newar.2009.02.001|arxiv=0902.0493 |bibcode=2009NewAR..53....1J }}</ref>

== Book ==
In 2020, Falcke co-published together with Jörg Römer the popular science book ''Licht im Dunkeln: Schwarze Löcher, das Universum und wir''. In English, it has been translated as ''Light in the Darkness – Black Holes, the Universe and Us''.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Falcke |first1=Heino |url=https://portal.dnb.de/opac.htm?method=simpleSearch&cqlMode=true&query=idn%3D123685294X |title=Light in the darkness: black holes, the universe, and us |last2=Römer |first2=Jörg |date=2021 |publisher=Wildfire |isbn=978-1-4722-7449-6 |series=The international bestseller |location=London}}</ref> The book also has translations in German, Dutch, Spanish, Italian and Finnish.

==Personal life==
Falcke is a devout Christian and serves as lay pastor in the [[Protestant Church in Germany]].<ref name=trouw>{{cite news|author=Ellen Nieuwenhuijze |url=http://www.trouw.nl/tr/nl/5091/Religie/article/detail/3409992/2013/03/15/Wetenschap-beantwoordt-niet-alles.dhtml |title=Wetenschap beantwoordt niet alles |language=Dutch |newspaper=[[Trouw]] |date=15 March 2013 |access-date=25 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Predigerinnen und Prediger |url=https://www.kirche-frechen.de/predigerinnen-und-prediger/ |access-date=14 November 2023 |website=Evangelische Kirchengemeinde Frechen |language=de-DE}}</ref> He views his faith as a way of achieving internal rest, as well as a motivation to conduct science.<ref name=trouw/>
